---
title: "Regions and products"
# The tables are wide: eight and nine columns, and one column per agreement
# category means they grow with the configured categories. The default
# article column would scroll them sideways.
format:
  html:
    page-layout: full
# This page is a report, not a notebook. The dashboard hides its cells
# because Quarto's dashboard format does; an ordinary page has to say so.
execute:
  echo: false
---

One row per region and product: how much of each source dataset reached this
site, and how the two flag sources line up across everything that did. The
dashboard answers the same question one profile at a time; this page is the
view from above, and it is the place to start when you do not yet know which
product is worth opening.

The data mode decides which profiles are counted. "NRT only" compares two
sets of automated flags. "Delayed mode" compares nrtqclib with input flags
that are likely to be an operator's decisions, which is a different
question. It holds the profiles with a delayed mode observation, those whose
temperature or salinity flags look like an operator's (see
[NRT and delayed mode](analyses-data-mode.qmd)), and CORA whole, since its
flags come from its own delayed mode QC. "Data mode unknown" holds the profiles whose files do not
say. The groups are kept apart unless you ask for all of them, and the last
section puts them side by side.

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// The same single module the dashboard imports. Resolving the specifier
// against document.baseURI keeps it working under any deployment path.
app = import(new URL("assets/js/app.js", document.baseURI).href)

catalog = app.loadCatalog()
variables = catalog.variables
statuses = catalog.statuses
mode_options = app.dataModeOptions(catalog)
// One row per region, product and data mode group: both the filtered tables
// and the side by side comparison are sums of these.
counted = app.regionProductTotals(variables, statuses)

// The rows of one data mode choice, one per region and product.
//
// The catalog lists every region and product; the query only returns the ones
// that have published profiles. Building the rows from the catalog and
// looking the counts up keeps a product whose profiles were all trimmed away
// visible as a zero rather than absent. The source totals come from the
// catalog too, per group, since the trimmed profiles are in no parquet.
function rowsFor(mode) {
  const bySlot = new Map();
  for (const found of counted) {
    if (mode !== app.ALL_MODES && found.data_mode !== mode) continue;
    const key = `${found.region}|${found.product}`;
    const sums = bySlot.get(key) ?? {};
    for (const [field, value] of Object.entries(found)) {
      if (field === "region" || field === "product" || field === "data_mode") {
        continue;
      }
      sums[field] = (sums[field] ?? 0) + Number(value ?? 0);
    }
    bySlot.set(key, sums);
  }

  return catalog.regions.flatMap((region) =>
    region.products.map((product) => {
      const found = bySlot.get(`${region.name}|${product.name}`) ?? {};
      const total = (field) => app.productTotal(product, field, mode);

      const row = {
        key: `${region.name}|${product.name}`,
        region: region.name,
        product: product.name,
        n_datasets: product.datasets.length,
        n_profiles: Number(found.n_profiles ?? 0),
        n_profiles_total: total("n_profiles_total"),
        n_obs: Number(found.n_obs ?? 0),
        n_obs_total: total("n_observations_total")
      };
      for (const variable of variables) {
        for (const status of statuses) {
          const field = `${variable.name}_${status.key}`;
          row[field] = Number(found[field] ?? 0);
        }
      }
      row.profile_share =
        row.n_profiles_total > 0 ? row.n_profiles / row.n_profiles_total : null;
      return row;
    })
  );
}

rows = rowsFor(summary_mode.key)

// Totals over every product, for the line under each table.
grand = {
  const sum = (field) => rows.reduce((n, row) => n + row[field], 0);
  const totals = {
    n_profiles: sum("n_profiles"),
    n_profiles_total: sum("n_profiles_total"),
    n_obs: sum("n_obs"),
    n_obs_total: sum("n_obs_total")
  };
  for (const variable of variables) {
    for (const status of statuses) {
      totals[`${variable.name}_${status.key}`] = sum(
        `${variable.name}_${status.key}`
      );
    }
  }
  return totals;
}

// Per 1,000 published observations, so products of very different sizes can
// be compared. Anything derived from a rate is null when there is nothing to
// divide by, rather than zero, which would read as "no disagreement".
function rate(count, observations) {
  return observations > 0 ? (1000 * count) / observations : null;
}

function share(value) {
  return value === null || value === undefined ? "" : `${(100 * value).toFixed(1)}%`;
}

function perThousand(value) {
  return value === null || value === undefined ? "" : value.toFixed(1);
}

// The categories where at least one source flagged the observation. The
// build marks them, so this page never has to name them.
flagged_statuses = statuses.filter((status) => status.flagged)
```

```{ojs}
viewof summary_mode = Inputs.select(mode_options, {
  label: "Data mode",
  format: (mode) => mode.label
})
```

```{ojs}
htl.html`<p class="nq-note">${summary_mode.description}</p>`
```

## What was published

Only profiles in which at least one source flagged at least one observation
are published, so the two "source" columns are the size of the dataset the
build read and the columns beside them are what survived that rule. A low
share is not a problem: it means the two sources agreed about most of the
dataset.

```{ojs}
app.tableView(rows, {
  columns: [
    { key: "region", label: "Region", align: "left", format: (value) => value },
    { key: "product", label: "Product", align: "left", format: (value) => value },
    { key: "n_datasets", label: "Files", title: "Datasets built into this product" },
    { key: "n_profiles", label: "Profiles", title: "Profiles published here" },
    {
      key: "n_profiles_total",
      label: "Source profiles",
      title: "Profiles in the source dataset"
    },
    {
      key: "profile_share",
      label: "Share",
      format: share,
      title: "Published profiles as a share of the source dataset"
    },
    { key: "n_obs", label: "Observations", title: "Observations published here" },
    {
      key: "n_obs_total",
      label: "Source observations",
      title: "Observations in the source dataset"
    }
  ],
  rowKey: "key",
  sortKey: "n_profiles",
  selectable: false,
  empty: "No products are published. Run the build step."
})
```

```{ojs}
htl.html`<p class="nq-meta">All products, ${summary_mode.label}:
  <strong>${app.formatCount(grand.n_profiles)}</strong> of
  ${app.formatCount(grand.n_profiles_total)} profiles published
  (${share(grand.n_profiles_total > 0 ? grand.n_profiles / grand.n_profiles_total : null)}),
  <strong>${app.formatCount(grand.n_obs)}</strong> of
  ${app.formatCount(grand.n_obs_total)} observations.</p>`
```

## How the two sources compare

Counts below cover the published profiles only, which is why "neither flagged"
is large: a published profile carries all of its observations, most of which
both sources call good. The rate in the last column is what makes products of
different sizes comparable.

```{ojs}
viewof summary_variable = Inputs.select(variables, {
  label: "Variable",
  format: (variable) => variable.label
})
```

```{ojs}
app.statusLegend(statuses)
```

```{ojs}
{
  const flagged = flagged_statuses;
  const name = summary_variable.name;

  // The bar is over the flagged categories alone. Drawn over all five it
  // would be a single grey block on every row, because a published profile is
  // mostly observations both sources call good.
  const shaped = rows.map((row) => {
    const n_flagged = flagged.reduce((sum, s) => sum + row[`${name}_${s.key}`], 0);
    const n_disagree = row[`${name}_original_only`] + row[`${name}_nrtqclib_only`];
    return {
      ...row,
      n_flagged,
      disagree_rate: rate(n_disagree, row.n_obs)
    };
  });

  return app.tableView(shaped, {
    columns: [
      { key: "region", label: "Region", align: "left", format: (value) => value },
      { key: "product", label: "Product", align: "left", format: (value) => value },
      {
        key: "n_flagged",
        label: "Flagged mix",
        align: "left",
        title: "How the flagged observations split between the cases",
        render: (value, row) =>
          app.compositionBar(
            flagged.map((status) => ({
              label: status.label,
              value: row[`${name}_${status.key}`],
              color: status.color
            })),
            { empty: "nothing flagged in this product" }
          )
      },
      ...statuses.map((status) => ({
        key: `${name}_${status.key}`,
        label: status.label,
        title: `${summary_variable.label}: ${status.label.toLowerCase()}`
      })),
      {
        key: "disagree_rate",
        label: "Disagree per 1,000",
        format: perThousand,
        title:
          "Observations the two sources disagree on, per 1,000 published observations"
      }
    ],
    rowKey: "key",
    sortKey: "disagree_rate",
    selectable: false,
    empty: "No products are published. Run the build step."
  });
}
```

```{ojs}
{
  const name = summary_variable.name;
  const n_disagree =
    grand[`${name}_original_only`] + grand[`${name}_nrtqclib_only`];
  return htl.html`<p class="nq-meta">All products, ${summary_variable.label.toLowerCase()}:
    <strong>${app.formatCount(n_disagree)}</strong> observations the two
    sources disagree on, ${perThousand(rate(n_disagree, grand.n_obs))} per
    1,000 published observations.</p>`;
}
```

## NRT against delayed mode

The same products split by data mode, one row per group a product has, for
the variable chosen above, each as a rate per 1,000 of its own published
observations. Where a product has delayed mode profiles, this is where the
difference shows: the automated tests and an operator tend to disagree in
other ways than two automated systems do.

```{ojs}
{
  const name = summary_variable.name;
  const groups = catalog.data_modes;
  const byGroup = new Map(
    groups.map((group) => [
      group.key,
      new Map(rowsFor(group.key).map((row) => [row.key, row]))
    ])
  );

  // One row per product and group, rather than one per product with every
  // group across: three groups of three columns do not fit beside the
  // product's name. A group the product has nothing in is left out, and the
  // table opens with each product's groups together, in catalog order.
  const shaped = rowsFor(app.ALL_MODES).flatMap((all, productIndex) =>
    groups.flatMap((group, groupIndex) => {
      const found = byGroup.get(group.key).get(all.key);
      if (!found || found.n_obs === 0) return [];
      const original = found[`${name}_original_only`];
      const computed = found[`${name}_nrtqclib_only`];
      return [
        {
          key: `${all.key}|${group.key}`,
          order: productIndex * groups.length + groupIndex,
          region: all.region,
          product: all.product,
          mode: group.label,
          n_profiles: found.n_profiles,
          n_obs: found.n_obs,
          original_rate: rate(original, found.n_obs),
          nrtqclib_rate: rate(computed, found.n_obs),
          disagree_rate: rate(original + computed, found.n_obs)
        }
      ];
    })
  );

  const text = (value) => value;
  return app.tableView(shaped, {
    columns: [
      { key: "region", label: "Region", align: "left", format: text },
      { key: "product", label: "Product", align: "left", format: text },
      { key: "mode", label: "Data mode", align: "left", format: text },
      { key: "n_profiles", label: "Profiles", title: "Published profiles" },
      { key: "n_obs", label: "Observations", title: "Published observations" },
      {
        key: "original_rate",
        label: "Original only per 1,000",
        format: perThousand,
        title: `${summary_variable.label} flagged by the input alone, per 1,000 observations`
      },
      {
        key: "nrtqclib_rate",
        label: "nrtqclib only per 1,000",
        format: perThousand,
        title: `${summary_variable.label} flagged by nrtqclib alone, per 1,000 observations`
      },
      {
        key: "disagree_rate",
        label: "Disagree per 1,000",
        format: perThousand,
        title: "The two together: observations the sources disagree on, per 1,000"
      }
    ],
    rowKey: "key",
    sortKey: "order",
    descending: false,
    selectable: false,
    empty: "No products are published. Run the build step."
  });
}
```
